title: What is known about 1RB1LD_1RC0RC_1LD0RE_0LB0LA_0RF1LA_---1RC
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB1LD_1RC0RC_1LD0RE_0LB0LA_0RF1LA_---1RC.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. After step 731,206 the left end of the tape never moves again. The head bounces between a point well inside the tape and the right end. On each round trip, everything right of the turning point is shifted right by exactly two cells, unchanged. Near the turning point, the irregular region on the left produces new material. So the right part of the tape is a frozen record of what that generator produced. Nothing about the generator's own rules is known, and no Lean rules beyond the bounded run are proved.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (F0); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 30,011 cells have been visited and 19,605 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Growth shape: fixed/sqrt
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape stopped growing in the second half of the run (bounded so far, or growing so slowly that no record fell in the last half). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.514).

claims.title: The stream is translated rigidly
claims.text: Between consecutive arrivals of the head at the right end, the tape right of a boundary cell is exactly the previous tape shifted right by 2 cells. This held for 436 of 436 round trips between steps 10<sup>8</sup> and 1.2·10<sup>8</sup>, with the boundary between cells 3,446 and 3,817 of a tape of 9,467 to 10,339 cells.

claims.title: The generator grows too
claims.text: For 39 round trips after each of 10<sup>6</sup>, 10<sup>7</sup>, 10<sup>8</sup> and 10<sup>9</sup> steps, the tape is 1,105, 3,161, 9,467 and 30,011 cells wide. The boundary of the rigid part lies between cells 777–808, 1,532–1,572, 3,446–3,531 and 11,845–11,890. In the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps the left end of the tape is last extended at step 731,206.

claims.title: Why it is hard
claims.text: The head drifts across the stream in a short local zigzag, not over a repeated word, so the shift rules used for other holdouts do not apply directly. The generator region has no visible block structure. The machine halts only when E reads 0 with a 0 to its right (F reading 0 is its only undefined transition). Whether the generator ever produces that is open.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. The open part is the generator: what it emits and how it changes.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. This machine has a generator on the left of its tape that keeps producing new, irregular material. On every round trip of the head, the material already produced is carried two cells further right, without a single change. This page runs the real machine in your browser and shows what is known.

facts.text: Round trips after which the stream is the old one shifted right by exactly 2 cells.
Growth of the tape per round trip.
No halt in the C simulator.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape stopped growing in the second half of the run (bounded so far, or growing so slowly that no record fell in the last half). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.514).
After 109 steps the tape spans 30,011 cells (496 left of the start, 21,252 right), with a density of 1s of 0.653.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

sections.heading: A generator and a conveyor
html: Follow the head after step 108. It runs from the right end of the tape back to about cell 3,400–3,600 in a tight zigzag (about 3.6 steps per cell), and then all the way back. One round trip takes about 43,000 steps.

Compare the tape at two consecutive arrivals at the right end. Beyond a boundary near the turning point, the new tape is the old one shifted right by exactly two cells, with no other change. This held for all 436 round trips between steps 108 and 1.2·108. So the right part of the tape is a conveyor: whatever the region near the turning point produces is carried off to the right and never touched again.
The stream itself looks irregular. A piece of it at step 100,130,996, cells 6,001–6,100:

html: <div style="overflow-x:auto"><table class="tbl"><thead><tr><th>step</th><th>tape width</th><th>rigid stream starts at cell</th></tr></thead><tbody>
The tape grows by two cells per round trip, so its width grows like the square root of the time. The generator, left of the boundary, keeps roughly 40% of it.

sections.heading: What would decide it
html: The conveyor is harmless: the stream is only copied. Everything rests on the generator, and the machine halts only when E reads 0 with a 0 to its right. A next step would be the transducer of one sweep across the stream, as rules on short words, proved in Lean. Then one could study the generator as a map from one round trip to the next.

summary: An irregular generator region whose output stream is carried rigidly to the right, two cells per round trip of the head; both the generator and the stream grow like the square root of the time.
family: irregular generator feeding a translated stream
